description: Native Memcheck cases. Each case runs one function under test so findings attribute unambiguously. Expectations live here rather than in code, so a compiler change that invalidates one surfaces as an unmet expectation.

cases.rationale: LLVM vectorizes the loop into two pcmpeqb compares with a single test, so no secret-dependent branch survives; this records the erasure rather than assuming a vulnerability
volatile loads block the vectorizer, so the per-byte branch survives and the secret reaches a conditional jump
cases.description: early-exit comparison with volatile per-byte loads

cases.rationale: accumulates over all 32 bytes with no secret-dependent branch or address
the secret becomes part of a load address; the instruction path is identical for every secret, so M1's comparator cannot see this and M2 can
reads every entry and selects with a subtle-derived mask, so neither the address nor any branch depends on the secret
cases.description: constant-time table scan with mask selection

cases.rationale: propagating secrecy through computation is expected and permitted; only branches and addresses are prohibited
proves declassification actually restores definedness rather than merely being called; without it, core::fmt would report spurious findings
cases.description: secret-derived result declassified, then branched on and printed

cases.rationale: must be silent; a finding here would mean detection is caused by something other than the secret marking, and a leak detected in the marked case would be meaningless
cases.description: instrumentation control: the vulnerable lookup with no marking

cases.rationale: Memcheck reports a real memory bug; it must be classified as a memory error and make the run inconclusive, never labelled a timing leak
cases.description: control: a genuine out-of-bounds read, unrelated to secrecy
